# Scope: com.noblemaster.lib.license (18 methods) and com.noblemaster.lib.script (11 methods).
# License (the 3 implementations repeat the same six members, so one naming covers them):
#   BootScreen.update() is the decisive reader: license.b() decides whether the game may start
#   (-> isValid), license.c() is passed to GameConfig.setMacBuild (-> isMacBuild) and license.a()
#   is logged as the license name (-> getName, "Accept" / "Expiring"). a(LicenseCallback) is the
#   asynchronous check entry point -> check ; e() is called from GameApplication.dispose
#   -> dispose. d() has no reader anywhere in the tree and is left unnamed.
#   ExpiringLicense's single field marks the 90-day trial as run out -> expired.
# ScriptStep: TutorialHintBox reads all four columns - a() goes through Messages.get
#   (-> getTextKey), b() is split on ':' and parsed as "L:10" / "C:..." (-> getPositionSpec),
#   c() being null decides isWaitingForConfirmation (-> getExpectedInput, the answer that advances
#   the step). The fourth string has no reader in this tree yet and is left unnamed.
# StepListener: the single callback fired when the player advances -> onStepChanged.
# StepSequencePlayer: a() / a(String) try to advance (the string form only when it matches the
#   current step's expected input) -> advance ; b() -> getCurrentStep ; a(ScriptStepList) ->
#   setSteps ; a(StepListener) -> addListener ; the private c() fans out to the listeners ->
# Nothing here is looked up by name (licenses are interfaces, tutorial steps come from a
# String[][] table), so renaming cannot change behaviour or data.
